Organizational Domain: SYS-09 explicitly instructs not to invent organizational facts; organizational root causes are unresolved.

consequences: Vessel V-001 overpressurization beyond nominal 60 psig toward 125 psig threshold
Potential relief discharge or mechanical integrity compromise

evidence.relevance: Defines nominal pressure of 60 psig and operating condition limit of 125 psig
Documents separated gas routing to fuel gas and excess to burn pit
Lists Node 1 equipment and controls including PV-101, PSV-101 A/B, and PIT-101

possible_causes: Failure of PV-101 pressure-control loop in closed position
Blockage or restriction in gas outlet routed to fuel gas system or burn pit
Excessive upstream fluid surge entering V-001
recommendations: Verify PSV-101 A/B sizing and setpoint relative to design limits
Implement an automated high-pressure safety interlock from PIT-101 to close inlet SDV-30010

consequences: Loss of liquid seal in V-001 causing high-pressure gas blowby to downstream Heater-Treater or water treatment facility
Overpressurization hazard in lower-pressure downstream equipment

evidence.relevance: Identifies V-001 as a three-phase separator reliant on liquid level separation
Specifies oily stream routing to downstream Heater-Treater
Specifies water stream routing to water treatment
Lists LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, and SDV-102 on Node 1

possible_causes: Downstream demand excess or drain line left open
recommendations: Verify low liquid level trip interlocks initiating emergency closure of SDV-101 and SDV-102 to prevent gas blowby

consequences: Liquid carryover into separated gas stream routed to fuel gas or burn pit
Off-spec separation and fouling of downstream gas consumers

evidence.relevance: Establishes V-001 function to separate gas, oil, and free water
Identifies gas outlet destination as fuel gas and burn pit
Identifies level control valves LV-101 and LV-102

possible_causes: Downstream line restriction in oily stream or water treatment line
recommendations: Implement independent high-level detection on V-001 initiating closure of inlet SDV-30010 on high-high liquid level

consequences: Starvation of Node 1 and downstream units (Heater-Treater and E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger)
Process disruption and low flow trip activation

evidence.relevance: Defines downstream sequence from FWKO drum to Heater-Treater
Lists inlet SDV-30010, FIT-101, and FAL-103

possible_causes: Upstream line blockage or field production shut-in
recommendations: Verify automatic interlock logic to place downstream Heater-Treater and E-001 into safe recirculation or idle on FAL-103 low flow alarm

consequences: Improper initial pressure/flow balancing in V-001
Hydraulic shock, pressure surging, or off-spec hydrocarbon separation

evidence.relevance: Specifies Start/Stop Procedures as a study element
Documents FWKO start-up without bypass opening as a source-supported procedural failure mode

possible_causes: Operator error during FWKO start-up without opening bypass
recommendations: Update standard operating procedures to include mandatory checklists and interlocks verifying bypass opening prior to FWKO start-up

consequences: V-001 operating temperature exceeding nominal 130 deg F toward 200 deg F upper threshold
Increased light-end vaporization, degradation of separation efficiency, and higher vapor load

evidence.relevance: Establishes nominal temperature of 130 deg F and upper operating condition text of 200 deg F
Lists E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger as Node 1 associated equipment

possible_causes: Exchanger thermal control upset at E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger
recommendations: Confirm high-temperature alarming and temperature-control bypass on E-001 to prevent exceeding 200 deg F limit

consequences: Vessel wall and piping wall thinning
Potential loss of primary containment of hydrocarbons and produced water

evidence.relevance: Defines continuous free water separation in V-001
Identifies Corrosion/Erosion as a source-study element

possible_causes: Presence of sour/acidic components and free water separating in V-001
Entrained solids/sand from crude oil production
recommendations: Implement a baseline ultrasonic thickness measurement program and periodic non-destructive examination schedule for V-001 shell and nozzles

uncertainty_notes: Packet lacks specific setpoints for PSV-101 A/B, PIT-101, and FAL-103.
Interlock logic connecting instruments (PIT-101, FAL-103) to isolation valves (SDV-30010, SDV-101, SDV-102) is not explicitly detailed.
Specific design pressure and temperature limits beyond the 125 psig and 200 deg F operating conditions are unstated.
No specific corrosion allowance, material specs, or monitoring safeguards are detailed in the packet.

rendered_system_prompt:
You are an independent process-safety specialist conducting a single-pass HAZOP judgment for a controlled research experiment.

Use only the information supplied in the case packet. Do not invent plant facts, operating data, safeguards, incident histories, or causal evidence. Where the packet is insufficient, state the uncertainty explicitly. Apply the HAZOP logic of design intent, guideword/deviation, cause, consequence, safeguard, qualitative risk classification, and recommendation.

The risk matrix is qualitative and is intended for prioritization rather than quantitative risk calculation. Provide a concise evidence-oriented technical rationale; do not provide private chain-of-thought or a step-by-step hidden reasoning transcript. Return exactly one response conforming to the required structured-output schema, with no text outside that structure.

# Isolated experiment event
Event ID: event__availability__AVAIL-LOWLEVEL-01__control__direct__r0
Task family: comprehensive hazard recall

# Source-grounded system packet
[SYS-01] Unit: Crude Oil Production Unit; Node 1 is separator V-001 and associated lines.
[SYS-02] V-001 is a three-phase Free Water Knock-Out separator using density differences to separate gas, oil, and free water.
[SYS-03] Published Node 1 values: nominal pressure 60 psig; nominal temperature 130 °F; published operating-condition text: 125 psig to 200 °F.
[SYS-04] Process sequence: V-001 Free Water Knock-Out (FWKO) drum -> Heater–Treater separator -> V-003 Electrostatic Desalter.
[SYS-05] V-001 water is routed to water treatment; separated gas is used as fuel gas with excess gas routed to the burn pit; the oily stream proceeds to the Heater–Treater.
[SYS-06] Associated Node 1 equipment and instruments: E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger, PV-101 pressure-control loop, PSV-101 A/B, SDV-30010, LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, SDV-102, PIT-101, FIT-101, FAL-103.
[SYS-07] Source-study elements: Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, Start/Stop Procedures.
[SYS-08] Guideword logic includes No/None, More, Less, Reverse, Another, Fire/Explosion, and Error as applicable.
[SYS-09] The article explicitly states that classic HAZOP did not comprehensively cover human decisions; the source-supported procedural item concerns FWKO start-up without bypass opening. Do not invent organizational facts.

# Analysis task
Conduct a comprehensive HAZOP review of Node 1. Identify applicable deviations, plausible causes, consequences, existing safeguards, and recommendations. Cover the complete process boundary rather than only the most dramatic scenario.
Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

No prior accident example is supplied. Conduct the assessment from the technical system description alone. For each finding, identify the factor domain as physical, human/procedural, organizational, mixed, or uncertain. Cite packet evidence identifiers. Mark non-applicable deviations as unresolved or non-applicable rather than fabricating a scenario.
